supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Energetic Halloween set with blistering Workingman's Dead era jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The early/late show erupts from a quiet matinee into a rowdy second half, highlighted by a soaring Cosmic Charlie/China Cat Sunflower flow and a seamless Good Lovin' jam. Garcia’s guitar tone is praised as perfect and his marathon playing drives the blues numbers. The soundboard capture preserves the raw energy with good clarity despite some post‑processing quirks.
ai_show_review.review: On October 31, 1970 the Grateful Dead turned Stony Brook’s Pritchard Gym into a Halloween playground. The early set starts modestly, but once the doors burst open the band launches into a high‑octane second half that still feels cohesive. Highlights include a blistering “Dark Hollow” that rolls straight into a fluid “Viola Lee Blues → Cumberland Blues” segue and then bursts out into a tight “Good Lovin'” jam. Garcia’s tone is described as perfect, his leads on the “Cumberland” jam are fiery, and he even adds a memorable pedal‑steel cameo with the New Riders later in the night. Mickey Hart’s drumming anchors the extended “The Other One” break, while the rhythm section keeps the blues numbers driving forward. The soundboard source captures the raw, ragged energy of the gym audience without sacrificing clarity, making this Halloween show one of the more exciting early‑70s performances despite a few low‑energy moments on quieter cuts.

best_recording.reason: Raw soundboard capture that balances the energetic late show jams with enough clarity to hear Garcia’s perfect tone and the seamless Dark Hollow → Viola Lee Blues → Good Lovin' flow.
